issues.legal_issue: A prolonged and lethargic acquisition process did not justify invoking urgency powers to exclude landowners’ opportunity to object to acquisition for construction of a jail.
material_facts: The acquisition was for construction of a district jail, a public purpose.
The State had proposed acquiring land for the jail several years before issuing the acquisition notifications.
After a further interval, the State began identifying suitable land, and it took about two years after the selection committee recommended land before the notifications were issued.
The State invoked the urgency provisions and excluded the statutory inquiry and hearing on landowners’ objections.
The landowners challenged the acquisition, and the High Court dismissed their challenge.
issues.conclusion: The State was not justified in invoking the urgency provision to dispense with the inquiry and hearing. The landowners could not be denied their right to object, and the appeal was allowed and the High Court’s judgment set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 17(1) and 17(4) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, urgency powers are exceptional, and exclusion of the inquiry under Section 5-A is not an automatic consequence of invoking Section 17(1). The Government must be satisfied that the time required for the inquiry would in all probability frustrate the public purpose; the public purpose alone does not establish urgency. The statutory power and its exercise are assessed in light of the circumstances and the Government’s application of mind. A prolonged, slow acquisition process can demonstrate that there was no urgency warranting denial of the hearing. The Court applied Radhy Shyam v. State of U.P. (2011) 5 SCC 553 and Dev Sharan v. State of U.P. (2011) 4 SCC 769; it distinguished Deepak Pahwa v. Lt. Governor of Delhi (1984) 4 SCC 308, where delay could increase an urgency that already existed, and noted that Chameli Singh v. State of U.P. (1996) 2 SCC 549 had been distinguished in Radhy Shyam.

rule.if: acquisition_challenge_appeal and jail_construction_project and urgency_authority_invoked and landowner_hearing_excluded and prolonged_state_inactivity

predicates.acquisition_challenge_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging the dismissal of a challenge to a land acquisition.
predicates.jail_construction_project: The land is proposed to be acquired for construction of a jail.
predicates.urgency_authority_invoked: The acquiring authority invokes an urgency procedure to proceed without the ordinary acquisition process.
predicates.landowner_hearing_excluded: The acquiring authority removes the landowners’ opportunity to object and be heard.
predicates.prolonged_state_inactivity: The government’s acquisition process includes substantial periods of delay or slow progress before the acquisition notifications are issued.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges an urgent acquisition for a jail, the landowners’ hearing is excluded, and the government’s process has been prolonged and inactive, the landowners retain their right to object and be heard.
